article_notes: Retrospective descriptive study of 108 PCR-positive B. gibsoni dogs at one emergency and specialty hospital in Hong Kong; data at presentation before diagnosis or specific treatment. No outcome, complication or mortality data. The only severity grouping is the HCT-based anaemia grade, cross-tabulated against thrombocytopenia grade (Table 3).

severity_definitions.label: severe vs moderate vs mild anaemia (vs normal HCT)
severity_definitions.definition: Anaemia graded by haematocrit: severe HCT < 20%, moderate 20% <= HCT < 30%, mild 30% <= HCT < 37.3%. Severe n=46, moderate n=22, mild n=21, normal HCT n=19.
severity_definitions.quote: Severity of anemia was classified based on HCT as severe (HCT < 20%), moderate (20% ≤ HCT < 30%), and mild (30% ≤ HCT < 37.3%).

associations.statistic: severe thrombocytopenia (PLT < 30 K/uL) in 17 dogs with severe anaemia vs 4 with mild anaemia (percentages are of all 108 dogs)
associations.location: Table 3 (columns: severe anaemia, moderate anaemia, mild anaemia, normal HCT)
associations.note: Cross-tabulation of anaemia grade by thrombocytopenia grade, no test. Other rows of Table 3 (moderate, mild, normal PLT, thrombocytosis) give the rest of the distribution; percentages in the table are of 108, not of the column. The 'Normal PLT' row prints 2 (25.0%) for moderate anaemia, an apparent typo. Authors comment that no dog had severe anaemia with normal platelets.
